theme: Currency and travel affordability crowdsourced data: Numbeo, Expatistan, hotel price indices (Hotels.com HPI archives), Trivago Hotel Price Index, Kayak price trackers
queries_run: gh search repos "hotel price index" --sort stars
gh search repos "cost of living index dataset" --sort stars
gh search repos "kayak price" flights --sort stars
gh search repos "purchasing power parity" dataset --sort stars
gh search repos "hotel prices" scraper --sort stars

candidates.name: griddedGDPpc
candidates.what_it_holds: Academic replication package (R + Matlab + Python scripts, no data files committed in repo root) for 'Downscaled gridded global dataset for GDP per capita at purchasing power parity (PPP) over 1990-2024, constant 2021 USD'. Global coverage, ADM0/ADM1/ADM2 admin levels plus gridded rasters (5 arcmin/30 arcmin/30 arcsec GeoTIFF) and GeoPackage+CSV tables, combining World Bank/IMF/CIA national data with OECD/Eurostat subnational detail. Actual output data lives on Zenodo (linked from paper: Kummu et al. 2025, Scientific Data 12:567), not in this GitHub repo. MIT-licensed code.
candidates.why_useful: Gives a country-by-country and subnational PPP-adjusted GDP per capita time series, which is a structural proxy for cross-border travel affordability and currency-adjusted consumer spending power feeding ABNB's international ADR/nights mix (relevant to gap themes on FX mix and regional consumer strength, e.g. overlapping with the existing FX-mix / consumer-strength-regional-split workstreams).
candidates.size_hint: code repo only (~20 scripts); actual data hosted on Zenodo, size unknown from this fetch
candidates.license: MIT (code); data license unspecified in README, check Zenodo

candidates.name: numbeopy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client for Numbeo's public cost-of-living pages via pd.read_html — pulls country-aggregate prices, per-city indices, and country-level indices on demand (no committed dataset, live pull only). Rate-limited, dependency-light. License 'Other' (CC BY-NC 4.0 per description, i.e. Numbeo's own data licence).
candidates.why_useful: Numbeo's cost-of-living and rent indices per city are a live, low-cost way to track relative travel/rent affordability across ABNB's top international markets, which could feed a cross-market affordability adjustment for ADR/nights forecasts.
candidates.license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (Numbeo data terms, per repo description)

candidates.name: scrape (Numbeo cost-of-living scraper)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper for Numbeo cost-of-living components by country/location; Apache-2.0 licensed, 13 stars. No dataset committed, scraper only.
candidates.why_useful: A ready scraper skeleton for the sanctioned-if-approved case of building a point-in-time Numbeo cost-of-living panel across ABNB markets (would need a human ToS decision per repo rules before running).

candidates.name: web-crawling-numbeo
candidates.what_it_holds: Scraper that pulls Numbeo cost-of-living data into a PostgreSQL database, dockerized. No data committed, method only. MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: Same class as above — a containerized pipeline for building a recurring Numbeo cost-of-living panel if a human authorizes scraping Numbeo.

candidates.name: numbeo_api_cost_of_living
candidates.what_it_holds: Unofficial Numbeo API wrapper, 20 stars (highest-starred Numbeo repo found). No committed dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Most-starred/likely most-maintained unofficial Numbeo client if the team ever gets ToS clearance to build a recurring cost-of-living/affordability panel.

candidates.name: numbeo-sql-importer
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Numbeo org repo ('Numbeo API Example – Retrieve Cost of Living for a City'); importer that loads Numbeo API responses into SQL. No bulk dataset committed — requires a paid Numbeo API key to pull data.
candidates.why_useful: This is the official/authorized path into Numbeo's data (via their paid API, not scraping), which sidesteps the ToS concern the repo rules flag for direct scraping of crowdsourced travel sites — worth flagging to a human as the 'ask for budget' option instead of an ad hoc scraper.

candidates.name: expatistan
candidates.what_it_holds: Ruby API client for Expatistan's cost-of-living comparison data (Numbeo's main crowdsourced competitor). No committed dataset. MIT license, low activity (last updated 2019).
candidates.why_useful: Only Expatistan-specific repo found; gives a second crowdsourced cost-of-living source (city-pair comparisons) distinct from Numbeo, useful for cross-checking any affordability index built from Numbeo alone.

candidates.name: trivago-Hotel-Price-Index-tHPI
candidates.what_it_holds: Described as 'Analysis of THPI 2015' (Trivago Hotel Price Index). README only surfaces a demo/visualization link, not a clear description of committed raw data files, years, or cities covered — could not confirm whether the underlying tHPI series is actually stored in the repo versus just an analysis of a single 2015 snapshot. Zero stars, last updated 2018, likely stale/abandoned.
candidates.why_useful: If the underlying Trivago Hotel Price Index data is genuinely present, it would be a rare committed copy of a defunct hotel price index series (Trivago's tHPI is no longer published) that could serve as a historical hotel-ADR comparator; flagged as uncertain and worth a manual look rather than confirmed high-value.

candidates.name: student-affordability-calculator
candidates.what_it_holds: Streamlit app combining live Numbeo cost-of-living data with European Central Bank FX rates to compute affordability across 326 cities in 107 countries for international students. No stored dataset — live-pull method combining two APIs.
candidates.why_useful: Demonstrates a working method for merging crowdsourced cost-of-living data with ECB FX rates into a single affordability score across 326 cities — a reusable pattern (not data) for an ABNB cross-market affordability index that already accounts for currency.

notes: This theme is structurally thin on GitHub: Numbeo, Expatistan, Hotels.com HPI, Trivago tHPI, and Kayak price trackers are all commercial crowdsourced sites with no public bulk-download culture, so almost every repo found is a scraper/API-client 'method' rather than a stored dataset, and most have single-digit stars. Trivago's Hotel Price Index and Hotels.com's HPI appear to be discontinued products with essentially no GitHub footprint at all (zero real hits beyond one ambiguous 2018 repo and one unrelated Airbnb-price-prediction repo whose description merely name-drops 'Hotel Price Index' loosely). Kayak price-tracker searches returned nothing usable — dead end. The one genuinely strong dataset surfaced (mattikummu/griddedGDPpc, a peer-reviewed downscaled global GDP-per-capita PPP dataset, Scientific Data 2025) is adjacent rather than on-theme: it is a macro/FX affordability proxy, not a travel-specific index, but it is a real, citable, code-complete academic package worth flagging to whichever scout owns fx_rates/macro_consumer_spend gaps. Recommendation for a human: if the team wants Numbeo/Expatistan data specifically, the fastest ToS-clean route is Numbeo's own paid API (numbeo/numbeo-sql-importer shows the pattern) rather than any of the unofficial scrapers found here, all of which touch numbeo.com directly and would need the same ToS sign-off the repo rules require before scraping non-sanctioned sites.
